filter.noteFilters: The preview is an approximation — the final color grade (LUT) is applied in the server-side render.
filter.noteEnhance: The preview is an approximation — the exact brightness/contrast/saturation/vignette is applied in the render (shared engine for video and photo).
filter.noteBackgroundFill: If the clip aspect doesn't match the canvas, the bars are filled black or with a blurred, fill version of the clip (real blur in the render).
filter.noteAnimate: One tap → ready-made camera move (with keyframes — refine further in the Precise adjust panel; live in preview and render).
filter.noteFaceBlur: The AI finds faces across several frames and blurs the bounding area (covering head movement too) — soft blur or mosaic. Burned in during the render; the preview shows it with a marker.
filter.noteSky: The AI recognizes the sky from a depth map and replaces it — the subject and foreground stay. The result becomes the clip's new source (undoable).
filter.noteLighting: Mood lighting in one tap — the render burns in a real split-tone color grade (shadows/midtones/highlights with separate colors); the preview approximates it with a tint. Combinable with enhancement.
filter.note3d: The clip tilts in space (real perspective warp in the render), the camera presets write keyframes — tilt and movement stay freely adjustable afterward. Tilt doesn't combine with the mask. On photos, 2.5D depth splits the image into layers via AI depth estimation, and the camera move comes to life with depth parallax in the rendered video (the preview moves the flat photo). 🌫️ portrait blur blurs the far content (in the preview too), while 🎬 focus pull floats the sharpness across the subject and background in the render. 🪄 subject cut-out places the photo's subject as a separate, transparent-background layer on the canvas — any new background can go beneath it.
filter.noteMaskEdit: When on, the mask frame and handles appear in the preview: drag the frame to move it, drag a corner to resize. For polygons, each vertex is draggable too.
filter.noteMask: The preview shows the mask outline and darkens the covered area — the real soft-edge cutout is made in the render.
filter.noteGreenScreen: The key color becomes transparent in the render (combinable with background fill: a black or blurred background goes behind it).

pip.cornerRoundingNote: “🔵 Circle” gives a full circle on a roughly square PiP — set the PiP size close to square for the webcam bubble.
pip.blendNote: The PiP blends with the main video (it doesn't cover it): ☀️ Screen = bright areas show through (light-leak, fireworks, light overlay), 🌑 Multiply = dark areas show through, Overlay/Lighten = contrast/double exposure. Baked into both preview and render.

precision.keyframeHint: Set the zoom/position on the canvas, then tap “◆ Keyframe here” — the clip animates between keyframes (the easing applies to the new keyframe). On a keyframed clip, pinch/drag also writes a keyframe.

shape.imageNote: Image-fill layer (logo/watermark) — size, corner radius, border and opacity are set below; the aspect ratio is kept by the image (contain).
shape.blendNote: The layer blends with the video below it — in the preview and in the render too.
shape.sizeStyleNote: You can position the shape by dragging it on the canvas — it burns into the rendered video exactly like this. In the render the shadow follows the shape's silhouette (on arrows and stars too).
shape.alignNote: While dragging, the layer snaps to the canvas center and third lines, the safe-zone borders, the center line of OTHER LAYERS and the equal spacing between them — the grid adds an even division on top of that.
shape.glowOutlineNote: Both follow the SILHOUETTE of the shape, so they work on the arrow, the star and the image-fill logo too — where a plain border doesn't. It shows exactly in the render; the preview approximates it.

speed.rampNotApplicable: Can't be applied to this clip (too short?).
speed.rampKeyframeWarning: The clip's keyframed motion will be removed with the ramp.
speed.rampBody: The clip is split into {{pieces}} variable-speed pieces; its length and the timing of other tracks don't change. The action can be undone.
speed.rampBlurNote: Motion blur on: fast pieces get blurred, slow ones get interpolated in-between frames (render only).
speed.curveNote: Drag the bars: each bar is the speed of an equal source segment. The scale is logarithmic, the line is 1× — above it speeds up, below it slows down. The clip's timeline length stays the same even if you redraw the curve.
speed.rampNote: The speed changes within the clip according to the curve (e.g. Hero: slowdown in the middle) — the clip's length doesn't change, and the pieces can be fine-tuned one by one afterwards. Works in preview and render; motion blur is only visible in the exported video.
speed.clipMotionBlurSpeedUp: When speeding up, it blends the dropped frames — the motion becomes smooth, not choppy.
speed.clipMotionBlurSlowDown: When slowing down, it computes in-between frames (motion interpolation) so the slow-mo stays smooth. Slower render.
speed.clipMotionBlurNeutral: It only has an effect if the clip is sped up or slowed down.
speed.enhancedAudioNote: 🎙️ The enhanced audio is also heard in the PREVIEW (the worker processes it with the same chain as the render). On the first playback the raw audio plays for a few seconds until it's ready.
speed.volumeAutomationNote: Volume automation: set the volume, move the playhead to the desired point, and hit ◆ — the volume fades between the keyframes.

text.noteTracking: 🎯 Pick a point: tap on the image what you want to track — the panel reopens and tracking starts from there. Or place the text on the subject, set the playhead to the start, and start it — the text takes over the point's motion, and if the subject moves closer/farther its size changes with it too (both in preview and render). With 🙂 face tracking you don't have to aim: the AI finds the face on the image and starts tracking from there. Combined with 3D text, the title “sits in the scene”.
